html:
The Dehcho Dene are the Dene of the Dehcho, the "big river", their name for the Mackenzie River, in the southwest of the Northwest Territories, Canada. They speak South Slavey, an Athabaskan language, and lived by hunting moose and caribou, trapping and fishing along the Mackenzie and Liard rivers.

The fur trade reached them around 1800, and Fort Simpson, where the Liard joins the Mackenzie, became the main Hudson's Bay Company post of the district. In 1921, after oil was found at Norman Wells, their leaders signed Treaty 11, which they say was a treaty of peace, not a sale of land. The Dehcho First Nations, which include the Acho Dene Koe, are still negotiating a land and self-government agreement with Canada. Their country includes the Nahanni National Park Reserve.
